reconcile.connective: Defenders read Mark's "in the days of Abiathar" as a loose time-marker, not a claim that Abiathar already held the office when David ate the bread.

discrepancy.connective: Bart D. Ehrman presses this as a plain factual error: Mark names Abiathar as the high priest, yet 1 Samuel 21 has his father Ahimelech in office at the time, and the simplest reading is that Mark misremembered.

skeptic.name: Bart D. Ehrman
skeptic.work: Misquoting Jesus: The Story Behind Who Changed the Bible and Why

excerpts.excerpt_text: the evangelist does not say that Abiathar was high priest, when David came and eat the showbread; he only says, "it was in the days of Abiathar the high priest" …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the name charge by parsing Mark's wording as a time-frame reference ('in the days of Abiathar') rather than an assertion that Abiathar held the office at the moment David ate — the standard 'epi Abiathar' harmonization and the very move the skeptic disputes. Strongest single reconcile; parity-capped on this discrepancy_first row.

pd_work.resource: John Gill, Exposition of the Entire Bible (1746-63), on Mark 2:25
pd_work.author: John Gill
pd_work.note: Gill treats this exact verse at length, working through the 'in the days of Abiathar' reading, the deputy/son-of-the-high-priest theory, and the dual-name proposal; the fullest PD harmonization of the Mark 2:26 / 1 Samuel 21:1 name discrepancy on the row.

link.title: GotQuestions: Why does Jesus call Abiathar the high priest in Mark 2:26, when 1 Samuel 21 indicates it was Ahimelech?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment citing both Mark 2:26 and 1 Samuel 21; harmonizes via naming Abiathar in anticipation of his future title or a shared priestly office.
